title: XboxPC Artifact Manifest — Official Xbox Series X OS Acquisition
evidence_basis: support.xbox.com fetch_page + github.com/microsoft/GDK API + learn.microsoft.com access-resources page + 6 corroborating web sources; sandbox egress blocked direct OSU1 download (see provenance)

official_sources: https://support.xbox.com/help/hardware-network/console/offline-system-update (Step 1: Download the Offline System Update file (OSU1))
http://www.xbox.com/xboxone/osu1 (short-redirect → download.microsoft.com/.../OSU1.zip — reported, not directly verified in sandbox)
artifacts.retrieval_environment: E2B sandbox iruwctpj94q0ohdxmj6c7 (Debian bookworm, GitHub egress allow-listed, Xbox/Microsoft download hosts blocked — see PROVENANCE.md §4)
artifacts.acquisition_detail: fetch_page to support.xbox.com succeeded (page shell retrieved, title verified); direct curl -I / urllib to www.xbox.com/xboxone/osu1 and download.microsoft.com failed with SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL/EOF (consistent with sandbox egress allow-list, not 404). No OSU1.zip was downloaded; no hash can be recorded here. Owner to retrieve in approved Windows+unrestricted-network environment.
artifacts.file_size_estimated_range: Approximately 4.8–6 GB (historical 2019 5.2 GB reported; current inferred from 6 GB NTFS USB requirement; no authoritative current size published on page shell)
artifacts.version_note: Support page is a rolling snapshot (Reddit 2019-10-11: 'files inside October update dated Sept 30'); version is embedded in payload metadata, not in page URL. No public build number advertised; must be extracted post-download from updater.xvd / payload manifest.
artifacts.sha256_note: Not recorded — file not acquired in this environment. Will be recorded in SHA256SUMS.txt upon owner retrieval (see PROVENANCE.md for verification steps).
artifacts.signature_evidence: Payload contains RM_Signature.bin at $SystemUpdate root (reported by futuretweets.com, twicethebits.com); Xbox console validates signature against hardware-fused Xbox retail keys (inferred from e-code failure paths; see RETAIL_OS_REQUIREMENTS.md). Direct signature verification not performed (no file).

internal_structure.top_level: $SystemUpdate/ (must be at NTFS USB root, exact case)
internal_structure.container_format: ZIP (external) → XVD (Xbox Virtual Disk) internals, variant of VHD

artifacts.includes_boot_chain: Not observably — relies on pre-existing console Boot ROM + Startup Troubleshooter; payload contains updater/system XVD slices, not firmware/bootloader for generic PC
artifacts.includes_required_firmware: No — SoC firmware, Boot ROM, board config absent from manifest
artifacts.requires_existing_xbox_installation: Yes — update is applied to existing System Update A/B partitions; version-check enforces newer-than-installed
artifacts.is_hardware_bound: Yes, Xbox-hardware-bound (Xbox Series X|S and Xbox One applicable, each console generation gated; not PC-portable per Support page segmentation)
artifacts.legally_redistributable: No — provided for repair of owned console; no redistribution license; see LICENSE-REVIEW.md
artifacts.can_support_pc_boot_objective: No — contributes analysis value but not an independent boot path
artifacts.access: public (requires Windows PC + 6 GB NTFS USB; no account needed)
evidence: web_search 'Xbox OSU1 offline system update' → futuretweets.com $SystemUpdate layout example
web_search → gbatemp.net/threads/496212 internal partition + XVD list (A/host.xvd ... updater.xvd, GPT GUIDs)
web_search → twicethebits.com OSU1 download URL pattern (xbox.com/xboxone/osu1)

artifacts.canonical_name: OSU2.zip (Intermediate update, original Xbox One only)
official_sources: https://support.xbox.com/help/hardware-network/console/offline-system-update (Section: Original Xbox One console only → Step 3)
artifacts.acquisition_detail: Not needed for Series X|S; documented only for completeness of offline update branching.

artifacts.canonical_name: OSU3.zip (Intermediate update, original Xbox One only)
official_sources: https://support.xbox.com/help/hardware-network/console/offline-system-update (Section: Original Xbox One console only → Step 3)

artifacts.acquisition_detail: GitHub API GET /repos/microsoft/GDK returned JSON id 348416224, private false, stars 1741; GET /repos/microsoft/GDK/contents listed 6 top-level entries; README.MD (17186 bytes) decoded from base64 confirmed GDK vs GDKX distinction.
artifacts.filename_as_distributed: N/A (GitHub repo + WinGet Microsoft.Gaming.GDK + NuGet Microsoft.GDK.Windows + vcpkg ms-gdk)
artifacts.is_entire_os: No — it is a game SDK, not a console OS
artifacts.legally_redistributable: Per LICENSE-EN-US.MD in repo (Other/NOASSERTION) — permissive for documented sample use but not for retail OS (which it is not)
artifacts.can_support_pc_boot_objective: No — provides PC game building, not console boot; Xbox graphics driver and console environment APIs are excluded (require GDKX)

artifacts.canonical_name: Secure Xbox Downloads / Microsoft Game Development Kit with Xbox Extensions (GDKX)
artifacts.acquisition_detail: Requires: Xbox development partner onboarding → Partner Center account (Xbox-provisioned) + valid GDK Agreement + Microsoft Entra ID tenant + MS rep enablement of Secure Downloads. Personal MSAs not supported. Even after onboarding, available resources are described as 'Latest release of software and recoveries of the GDK, offline docs, Submission Validator' — no documented guarantee of retail console OS image for generic PC.
artifacts.is_entire_os: Unknown — even secure inventory does not advertise PC-bootable retail OS; investigation would require onboarding and insider inspection, which is blocked without approval
artifacts.can_support_pc_boot_objective: Unproven — no public description promises PC-bootable retail OS exists even under GDKX

verdict.can_legitimately_obtain_complete_retail_: No — no public artifact demonstrated to be a complete, independently bootable retail OS image. Only OSU1 update payload is publicly obtainable; GDK is game SDK not OS; GDKX potential is unproven even under authorization.
verdict.can_verify_authenticity: Yes for OSU1 (signature RM_Signature.bin, Microsoft domain) — but verification proves it is a legitimate UPDATE, not a legitimate FULL OS.
